title: Orchestrate credentialed artifact publish with performance-profile reconciliation
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Build a CI/CD orchestrator that produces cryptographically credentialed model artifacts and performance profiles, automatically reconciles published profiles against short-window runtime observations, and gates promotion to pinned releases. This ticket creates a pipeline (build -> reproducible hash -> SBOM -> sign -> profile compute -> publish -> pin candidate) plus a reconciliation loop that compares published profiles to live telemetry using a golden query set. The pipeline must emit provenance metadata consumable by the runtime and Console, and allow safe automated retraction/rollback if reconciliation detects regressions.

Background: Current onboarding is partially manual: builds get produced and performance profiles are uploaded by hand to the profile catalog. This adds latency and creates drift between claimed profiles and actual runtime behavior (sequence length distribution, latency p50/p95). We need a single authoritative flow where each published profile is bound to a signed artifact and automatically validated against sampled live traffic or shadow traffic before being used for pinning into production pools.

Non-goals: full canary automation across Dedicated clusters (that will be follow-up). This ticket focuses on artifact credentialing and reconciliation gating for profile publication and pinning; manual canary steps remain available as opts-in actions.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline defined in model-cd repo that starts from a model build output and ends with a profile publish candidate (staged namespace)
Build artifacts include reproducible content-hash, SBOM, and a cosign-compatible signature referencing KMS/HSM key ID
Computed performance profile includes token-level cost estimates, latency distributions, and a canonical golden-query eval set result

Reconciliation job runs for the first 24 hours after publish and compares profile predictions to runtime telemetry; any regression above thresholds triggers automated pin hold and creates an incident entry
Console and model registry display provenance metadata (build hash, signature, profile version, reconciliation status) for every published profile
Rollforward and automated retraction APIs exist: a single API call can mark a profile deprecated and revert pinned model references within committed pools
End-to-end integration test that simulates a degraded kernel (adds synthetic 50ms latency) and verifies reconciliation detects the regression and prevents pin promotion
implementation_notes: Pipeline stages: (1) hermetic build -> (2) sbom + ml-metadata snapshot -> (3) reproducible hash + artifact bundle -> (4) sign with cosign/KMS -> (5) compute perf profile using golden-query set on CI infra -> (6) publish to profile-catalog (staged) with metadata -> (7) reconciliation monitor (24h) -> (8) auto-publish/pin or hold
Use cosign for signatures and store signature pointers and key IDs in the profile manifest; integrate with cloud KMS and on-prem HSM for Private installs
Profile compute must be deterministic: fix seeds, dataset slice selection, and evaluation harness versions; record CI job id and container image used

Reconciliation compares: latency p50/p95, throughput for common sequence buckets (0-128,129-512,512+), and token-level cost estimates. Threshold defaults: latency p95 regression > 15% or +30ms, cost delta > 10%

Telemetry sources: runtime metrics exporter (prometheus), Console sample traces, and the profile-catalog shadow-run harness. Ensure sampling preserves privacy (no PII), use hashed request fingerprints
Expose reconciliation outcomes via automated GitHub statuses and create a single Slack channel alert with runbook link
Maintain backward compatibility: if a model artifact lacks a signed profile, the pipeline will still publish but mark "profile: unsigned" and disallow automatic pinning
Metrics emitted: time-to-publish (mins), time-to-sign (mins), reconciliation-pass-rate, number of auto-retractions per month
updates: 2026-02-12: Scoping meeting with PM, Runtime, and Console. Agreed to keep canary orchestration as separate follow-up. Decided reconciliation window = 24h by default. Action: write the reconciliation runbook (assigned Nora Patel).

2026-02-18: Prototype pipeline in model-cd branch 'credentialed-publish' created. Build produces SBOM and content hash; cosign integration pending KMS key provisioning. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-cd/pull/742

2026-02-24: Architecture review: runtime team raised concern about sampling overhead. Decision: use asynchronous sampling at 1% by default and allow higher sampling for canary runs. Added requirement to respect customer privacy and masking rules.

2026-03-03: First end-to-end run in staging: build -> sign (test key) -> profile compute -> publish (staged namespace). Reconciliation job executed and matched expectations for sequence buckets. Observed discrepancy in long-seq latency for one kernel; opened issue ENG-90768 to investigate kernel selection mismatch.

2026-03-10: Legal/security completed initial review of signatures and provenance metadata. Need to add key rotation doc to runbook. Security reviewer: Liam O'Connor. Next: request HSM access for Private pilot customers.

2026-03-12: Implemented GitHub status checks and Slack alerts. Console display mockups reviewed by PM and Design; small feedback to include 'reconciliation heatmap' in profile detail panel (DES-21792).
risks: False positives in reconciliation could block valid releases — mitigation: conservative thresholds and manual override path
Signing key compromise — mitigation: KMS/HSM, short rotation, and cross-signing audit
Sampling bias in telemetry leading to missed regressions — mitigation: configurable sampling buckets and golden-query shadow runs
Performance overhead if reconciliation shadow runs are too heavy — mitigation: limit to lightweight metrics and 1% sampling default
review_feedback: PM Nora Patel: emphasise clear rollback UI in Console and API for platform teams
Runtime lead Sofia Martinez: require reconciliation to surface kernel mismatch hints (which kernel was used during profile compute)
Security Liam O'Connor: add explicit key-rotation doc and HSM TODOs for Private installs
